To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
30 of 68 yeast ribosomal proteins are acetylated at their N-termini, and that 24 of these are NatA substrates and 4 are NatB substrates.

the N-terminal acetylations of 30 ribosomal proteins are NatA substrates (unacetylated in ard1-Δ mutants), NatB substrates (unacetlylated in nat3-Δ mutants), and NatD substrates (unacytelyated in ard1- and mak3- mutants).
NatA, NatB, and NatD acetylate ribosomal proteins in yeast.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the action of N-terminal acetyl transferases (NATs) in yeast.
the identification and characterization of the substrates of all three known N-terminal acetyltrans-ferases in yeast.
the action of NatA, NatB, and NatD on the N termini of yeast ribosomal proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the yeast ribosomes contain NatA and NatB substrates and that they contain a NatD substrate, but that they do not contain a NatC substrate.

the N-terminal acetylations of the ribosomal subunits are mainly NatA substrates (Ard1p and Nat3/Nat3p) and NatD substrates (Ary1p and Nat4p) and that the NatB substrates (Nat10p and Mak3p) are minor.
the yeast ribosomal proteins are substrates for the NatA, NatD, and NatB acetyltransferases and, possibly, for the NatC acetyltransferase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NatA and NatD are the predominant N-terminal acetyltrans- ferases for the N-terminal acetylations of ribosomal proteins in yeast.
24 NatA substrates (80%) and 4 NatB substrates (13%) were found among the 30 N-terminal acetylated ribosomal proteins (41%).
NatA substrates are the most common, followed by NatD, and NatB substrates being least abundant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N-terminal acetylome of the yeast ribosome is dominated by NatA substrates and is relatively simple, with only a few NatB, NatD, and no NatC substrates.

NatA and NatB are the main N-terminal acetylases of yeast ribosomal proteins, and that NatA is the predominant acetylase for most ribosomal proteins, whereas NatB acetylates only a few ribosomal proteins, mainly those that have Ac-Met- termini.
N-terminal acetylases play an essential role in ribosome function, and that this role is largely confined to NatA substrates.
